description: Count business days between two dates, or find the date a number of business days before or after a date, skipping Saturdays, Sundays and US federal holidays on the days they are observed. Send start and either end (to count) or add_business_days (to step; negative steps back). Holidays follow 5 U.S.C. 6103 as federal offices observe them (Saturday holiday on the Friday before, Sunday holiday on the Monday after) or, if you choose, as the Federal Reserve Banks do (a Saturday holiday is not moved). Get back the count both ways (both dates included, and start left out), or the result date, with the weekend days and every holiday skipped by name and date. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/business-days). Labels are your own text: emails, web addresses and long digit runs are refused. Not legal, tax or financial advice.

add_business_days.description: To step: how many business days after start (negative: before start), not counting start itself. 1 = the next business day. Not 0.

end.description: To count: the end date, YYYY-MM-DD, on or after start. Send end or add_business_days, not both.

holidays.description: federal_offices (default): 5 U.S.C. 6103 holidays, Saturday ones on the Friday before and Sunday ones on the Monday after. federal_reserve_banks: the same holidays, Sunday ones on Monday, Saturday ones not moved.

label.description: Optional label, e.g. 'notice period' (your own text, echoed).
